author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: page is int-typed via @RequestParam so Spring rejects non-numeric input with HTTP 400 before the handler runs — no string injection surface on the pagination parameter
lastName reaches the datastore only through the Spring Data derived query findByLastNameStartingWith, which parameterizes the bind value — no SQL injection introduced
clamp of page<1 to 1 removes the negative-index path into PageRequest.of, closing the prior unhandled IllegalArgumentException (500) without adding new trust boundaries
getOffset() in Spring Data computes offset as a long, so a large int page value cannot integer-overflow the SQL OFFSET; an out-of-range page returns an empty page rather than an error
no change to authn/authz, serialization, file I/O, or dependencies; attack surface is unchanged apart from the hardened input path

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: Variable named `tasks` holds a `Page<Owner>`; the name `tasks` has no domain meaning here and misleads the next reader. This is a pre-existing pattern across the test class that the new test followed consistently, so it is not a blocker, but worth correcting in place. Rename to `ownersPage` or `results` for all occurrences in the method.
findings.fix: Rename `tasks` to `ownersPage` in the new test method body (line 153): `Page<Owner> ownersPage = new PageImpl<>(List.of(george(), new Owner())); when(this.owners.findByLastNameStartingWith(anyString(), any(Pageable.class))).thenReturn(ownersPage);`

findings.description: The test name promises `ReturnsFirstPage` but the only assertions are `status().isOk()` and `view().name("owners/ownersList")`. Neither confirms that the repository was called with page index 0 (the first page). The fix does prevent the exception, but the spec claim in the name goes unverified. Adding a `verify(owners).findByLastNameStartingWith(anyString(), argThat(p -> p.getPageNumber() == 0))` would make the test a true specification of the clamping behaviour. Not a blocker — the existing test still catches the regression — but the name over-promises what is asserted.

Why-comment (`// treat any page below 1 as the first page`) makes the intent legible cold without over-explaining
Method length, single responsibility, and early-return shape are all within the project norm

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Test method name processFindFormWithPageBelowOneReturnsFirstPage violates the BDD naming school mandated for tests written from 2026-07-31 onward. The brief (§ Test Naming) requires the{Subject}Should{Outcome} — the name must read as a specification, not a description of what method is called.

The test asserts HTTP 200 and the owners/ownersList view name but never asserts that model attribute currentPage equals 1. The core specification of the fix — that page=0 is clamped to page 1 visible in the model — is not expressed. A passing test for a controller that returned currentPage=0 would still satisfy these assertions.
findings.fix: Add .andExpect(model().attribute("currentPage", 1)) to the MockMvc assertion chain.

findings.description: The production fix clamps any page < 1 (covering zero and all negative integers) but the new test exercises only page=0. Negative values such as page=-1 represent a distinct input category and are untested. The brief (§ Boundary Testing) requires boundary inputs to be covered. A @ParameterizedTest with page=0, page=-1, and page=Integer.MIN_VALUE would specify the full boundary.
findings.fix: Convert to @ParameterizedTest @CsvSource covering page=0, page=-1, and page=Integer.MIN_VALUE, or add a dedicated negative-value test.

approved_aspects: Tests pass cleanly — the fix prevents the IllegalArgumentException that PageRequest.of(-1, 5) would otherwise throw
Mock usage follows the pre-existing suite pattern; the brief explicitly tolerates this for the existing suite
No new mock library dependencies introduced
The happy-path page=1 case in processFindFormSuccess continues to pass unaffected
